ruling.recommended_action: Issue a S$5.51 voucher refund for the unexempted detour and record the RD-1 breach; no account flag warranted.

segment_findings.reason: Exit off the planned route at ~09:57 (GPS 1.2878,103.8453 → 1.2895,103.8430 → 1.2874,103.8406) with no chat notice before the deviation; driver's obligation under RD-1 to take the shortest and most direct route absent reasonable cause is unmet. Not covered by RD-5 (no consent before the change).

NW loop through Jurong West/Boon Lay from ~09:58 to 10:06. RD-4 is factually satisfied (LTA 'Vehicle breakdown on Ayer Rajah Expressway' reported 09:47, within 300 m of the AYE alignment being avoided; AYE speed band 5), but RD-5 requires the rider's agreement before leaving the optimum route, and consent was only given at 10:06:40. This initial, unannounced ~2.1 km deviation remains unexempted under RD-1/RD-2.

Remainder of the loop after the rider's 10:06:40 'Sure, go ahead', which is a confirmed pre-route-change agreement covering the AYE-avoiding loop via Prince George's Park (RD-5), and is in any event backed by the LTA breakdown incident + speed band under RD-4(a)/(b).

rejected_claims.reason: The LTA breakdown incident does support avoiding the AYE (RD-4(a)), but the driver left the optimum route and completed ~2.1 km of the diversion before obtaining the rider's consent; RD-5 requires agreement before the route change, so the earlier portion is not exempt under RD-1/RD-2.

The rider's claim of paying 'more than the estimate' is only partly made out: the metered fare legitimately exceeds the app quote because RydeTAXI bills by meter, and most of the deviation is covered by RD-4 and RD-5; only the unexempted detour km (× distance rate) is refundable.
